rows.name: Lake Kariba 2024
rows.next_model: El Nino water-balance ensemble (strictly forward, ENSO state known at the time)
rows.notes: Ensemble first alarm Jul 2023 came from low storage under a neutral ONI; El Nino analogs used from Aug 2023, P(below 20%) = 0.8 in Oct-Dec 2023. The ML model expected the usual rainy-season recovery and fired only in Mar 2024.

summary.headline: Kariba 2024 was flagged in Jul 2023 by the El Nino reservoir model, 5 months before the official water cut; the country monthly model caught 1 of 5 other crises (Vietnam 2023). Short-range monthly country forecasts have little skill; the early warning comes from reservoir storage and the El Nino signal.

country_model.threshold_rule: Lowest threshold (grid 0.05-0.95) giving <= 1 false alarm per country per 5 calm years. Calm issue months have no observed shortfall in the next 6 months. An alarm covers a 6-month window, so 6 alarm-months in calm periods count as one false alarm: rate = (calm alarm-months / 6) / (calm months / 60). Equivalent to a false-positive rate of <= 10% on calm months.

false_alarms.kariba_next_model_definition: Seasons Oct-Dec 1995-2025; alarm = P(below 20%) > 0.5 on any Oct-Dec issue; event = below 20% at any point Apr-Dec of the following year.

notes: lead_months = months from the first Patronus alarm (either model) to crisis onset.
lead_vs_official_months is positive when Patronus fired before the first official warning.

Robustness test (3-month seasonal target, specified after the primary analysis): it caught Ecuador's April 2024 wave 4 months ahead (same month as the official warning) and missed the rest, including Vietnam 2023.
The country model's alarm threshold was chosen on the same out-of-fold predictions used to measure leads, so its catches are optimistic.
